claims.quote: Mount Ararat was the main home of the Vishap. The volcanic character of the Araratian peak and its earthquakes may have suggested its association with the Vishap.

claims.statement: Sometimes with its children the vishap stole toddlers and left a small evil spirit of its brood instead; by ancient belief it rose to the sky or came down, causing thunderstorms, whirlwinds and swallowing the sun (an eclipse).
claims.statement_id: Kadang bersama anaknya, vishap mencuri anak kecil dan menggantinya dengan roh jahat kecil dari keturunannya; menurut kepercayaan kuno ia naik ke langit atau turun ke bumi, menimbulkan badai petir, angin puting, dan menelan matahari (gerhana).
claims.quote: Sometimes with its children, the Vishap used to steal children or toddlers and put a small evil spirit of their own brood in their stead. According to ancient beliefs, the Vishap ascended to the sky or descended therefrom to earth, causing thunderous storms, whirlwinds, and absorption of the sun (causing an eclipse).

claims.statement: The dragon was worshipped in several Eastern countries as a symbol of water, fertility and wealth, later a frightful symbol of power; ancient legend has it fight Vahagn the Dragon Slayer.
claims.statement_id: Naga ini dipuja di sejumlah negeri Timur sebagai lambang air, kesuburan, dan kekayaan, kemudian menjadi lambang kekuasaan yang menakutkan; menurut legenda kuno ia bertarung dengan Vahagn Pembunuh Naga.
claims.quote: The dragon was worshipped in a number of Eastern countries, symbolising the element of water, fertility and wealth, and later became a frightful symbol of power. According to ancient legends, the dragon fought Vahagn the Dragon Slayer.

claims.statement: In Yerevan stands a statue of Vahagn, who slew the vishap, by Karlen Nurijanyan and Nerses Charkhchyan.
claims.statement_id: Di Yerevan ada patung Vahagn, pembunuh vishap, karya Karlen Nurijanyan dan Nerses Charkhchyan.
claims.quote: There is a statue to Vahagn, who slew the Vishap, in Yerevan by Karlen Nurijanyan and Nerses Charkhchyan.

claims.statement: The vishap is a figure of Armenian mythology closely linked with water; it is a legendary animal.
claims.statement_id: Vishap adalah tokoh mitologi Armenia yang erat kaitannya dengan air; ia hewan legendaris.
claims.quote: Վիշապ, հայկական դիցաբանական կերպար, որը սերտորեն կապված է ջրի հետ: Վիշապը առասպելական կենդանի է:

claims.statement: Yalmauz (from Bashkir ialmau, "to enclose", and auyz, "mouth"; literally "the one who swallows everything") is an evil demon in Bashkir mythology.
claims.statement_id: Yalmauz (Ялмауз; dari bahasa Bashkir ialmau, "melingkupi", dan auyz, "mulut"; harfiah "yang menelan segalanya") adalah iblis jahat dalam mitologi Bashkir.
claims.quote: Ялмауз (ялмауыҙ, от баш. ялмау — охватывать и ауыҙ — рот; букв. — заглатывающий всё) — злой демон в башкирской мифологии.

claims.statement: Yalmauz appears in Bashkir tales such as "Karasa-batyr" and "Altyndugha-batyr".
claims.statement_id: Yalmauz muncul dalam dongeng Bashkir seperti "Karasa-batyr" dan "Altyndugha-batyr".
claims.quote: Ялмауз встречается в башкирских сказках («Ҡараса батыр» — «Караса-батыр», «Алтындуға батыр» — «Алтындуга-батыр» и др.).

claims.statement: The demon Yalmauz is a 7-, 9- or 12-headed (seven, nine, twelve) serpent-like creature living in a garden it planted; in tales the batyrs rescue the maidens it holds by fighting and killing it.
claims.statement_id: Iblis Yalmauz adalah makhluk mirip ular berkepala 7, 9, atau 12 (tujuh, sembilan, dua belas) yang tinggal di kebun yang ditanaminya sendiri; dalam dongeng para batyr menyelamatkan gadis tawanannya dengan bertarung dan membunuhnya.
claims.quote: Злой демон Ялмауз представляет собой 7-, 9- или 12-головое змееподобное существо, живущее в саду, который он сам засадил деревьями. Обычно в сказках батыры, спасая девушек, находящихся в неволе у Ялмауза, вступают с демоном в поединок и убивают его.

claims.statement: By belief Yalmauz is also a man-eating sorcerer, a vampire abducting babies and girls; according to M. A. Kulaev it is described as a wide-mouthed old woman like a myaskai.
claims.statement_id: Menurut kepercayaan, Yalmauz juga penyihir pemakan manusia, vampir yang menculik bayi dan gadis; menurut M. A. Kulaev ia digambarkan sebagai perempuan tua bermulut lebar mirip myaskai.
claims.quote: По поверьям, Ялмауз также — колдун-людоед, вампир, который похищает младенцев и девушек. Согласно М. А. Кулаеву, Ялмауз описывается как большеротая старая женщина, похожая на мяскай.

claims.statement: For example, in Uyghur yalmauz means "dragon".
claims.statement_id: Misalnya, dalam bahasa Uighur yalmauz berarti "naga".
claims.quote: Например, в уйгурском языке ялмауз означает «дракон»

claims.statement: Yalmavuz (Tatar Җалмавыз) is a giant of Turkic and Altai mythology, also called Calmağus, Yelmeves or Yalmuz; a huge human-shaped tale creature with three, seven or 12 (twelve) heads, black or yellow, sometimes synonymous with Yelbegen; giants are hostile to horses and eat people.
claims.statement_id: Yalmavuz (Tatar: Җалмавыз) adalah raksasa dalam mitologi Turkik dan Altai, juga disebut Calmağus, Yelmeves, atau Yalmuz; makhluk dongeng sangat besar berwujud manusia dengan tiga, tujuh, atau 12 (dua belas) kepala, berwarna hitam atau kuning, kadang sinonim Yelbegen; para raksasa memusuhi kuda dan memakan manusia.
claims.quote: Türk ve Altay mitolojisinde Dev. Calmağus veya Yelmeves de denir. “Yalmuz” olarak da bilinir. Çok büyük masal yaratığı. İnsan biçimlidir. Üç, yedi veya 12 başı vardır. Siyah ya da sarı renklidir. Kimi zaman Yelbegen ile eşanlamlı olarak kullanılır. Devler, atlara düşmandır. Ayrıca insanları yerler.

claims.statement: According to Radloff, the Teleut Yilbegen corresponds to the Kyrgyz "Jalmaus".
claims.statement_id: Menurut Radloff, nama Yilbegen pada orang Teleut sepadan dengan "Jalmaus" pada orang Kirgiz.
claims.quote: Radlofa göre, Teleğütlerdeki Yilbegen ile Kırgızlardaki "Jalmaus" adı birbirlerini karşılamaktadır.

claims.statement: Złota Kaczka (Polish for "Gold Duck") is the heroine of a folk tale retold in many settings by many writers, including the poet Artur Oppman.
claims.statement_id: Złota Kaczka (bahasa Polandia untuk "Bebek Emas") adalah tokoh utama dongeng rakyat yang diceritakan dalam banyak latar oleh banyak penulis, termasuk penyair Artur Oppman.
claims.quote: (Polish for "Gold Duck") is the heroine of a folk tale which has been recounted with many settings and by many writers, including the Young Poland poet Artur Oppman.

claims.statement: The story is now most closely associated with Warsaw, Poland.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini kini paling erat dikaitkan dengan Warsawa, Polandia.
claims.quote: The story has come to be most closely associated with Warsaw, Poland.

claims.statement: In one version the Gold Duck, a princess bewitched by an evil sorcerer, swam in a lake beneath Warsaw's Ostrogski Castle (now the Fryderyk Chopin Museum).
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu versi, Bebek Emas adalah putri yang disihir penyihir jahat dan berenang di danau di bawah Kastel Ostrogski di Warsawa (kini Museum Fryderyk Chopin).
claims.quote: In one version the Gold Duck, a princess who had been bewitched by an evil sorcerer, swam in a lake beneath Warsaw's Ostrogski Castle (now home to the Fryderyk Chopin Museum).

claims.statement: She could be restored to human form only by someone spending 100 (a hundred) ducats a day for three straight days without sharing it.
claims.statement_id: Ia hanya bisa kembali ke wujud manusia bila seseorang membelanjakan 100 (seratus) dukat sehari selama tiga hari berturut-turut tanpa membaginya dengan siapa pun.
claims.quote: She could be restored to human form only by someone who could spend 100 ducats a day over three consecutive days, without sharing this fortune with anyone.

claims.statement: A soldier nearly succeeded, but as the third day closed he gave his last grosz to a beggar, and the Gold Duck vanished with the castle.
claims.statement_id: Seorang prajurit hampir berhasil, tetapi menjelang akhir hari ketiga ia memberikan grosz terakhirnya kepada pengemis, dan Bebek Emas lenyap bersama kastelnya.
claims.quote: A certain soldier was close to succeeding. But as the third day was drawing to a close, he gave the last grosz (penny) to a beggar, and the Gold Duck vanished together with the castle.

claims.statement: The oldest evidence of the gold duck legend in Warsaw dates from 1830, when Andrzej Słowaczyński used its plot in the vaudeville Chłopiec studukatowy.
claims.statement_id: Bukti tertua legenda bebek emas di Warsawa berasal dari tahun 1830, ketika Andrzej Słowaczyński memakai alurnya dalam vaudeville Chłopiec studukatowy.
claims.quote: Najstarszy dowód na funkcjonowanie legendy o złotej kaczce w Warszawie pochodzi z 1830 roku. Wtedy to Andrzej Słowaczyński wykorzystał jej fabułę w wodewilu Chłopiec studukatowy.

claims.statement: In 1852 Roman Zmorski recorded the legend in Podania i baśnie ludu w Mazowszu; in his version the gold duck lives in the flooded cellars of the ruined palace of the Prince de Nassau.
claims.statement_id: Pada 1852 Roman Zmorski mencatat legenda ini dalam Podania i baśnie ludu w Mazowszu; dalam versinya bebek emas tinggal di ruang bawah tanah yang tergenang di istana runtuh milik Pangeran de Nassau.
claims.quote: W 1852 roku legendę przytoczył Roman Zmorski w swoich Podaniach i baśniach ludu w Mazowszu. W jego wersji złota kaczka żyje nie pod Zamkiem Ostrogskich, lecz „na Dynasowskiej Górze”, w zalanych piwnicach zrujnowanego pałacu księcia de Nassau.

claims.statement: The zana (Gheg Zanë, Tosk Zërë) is a nymph-like figure of Albanian mythology tied to mountains, springs, streams, forests, plants, animals, human vital energy and sometimes destiny; Zana e Madhe ("the Great Zana") is thought to have been an Illyrian goddess equivalent to the Greek Artemis and Roman Diana.
claims.statement_id: Zana (Zanë dalam Gheg, Zërë dalam Tosk) adalah sosok mirip nimfa dalam mitologi Albania yang terkait gunung, mata air, sungai, hutan, tumbuhan, hewan, energi hidup manusia, dan kadang takdir; Zana e Madhe ("Zana Agung") diduga dewi Iliria setara Artemis Yunani dan Diana Romawi.
claims.quote: is a nymph-like figure in Albanian mythology and folklore, usually associated with mountains, springs and streams, forests, vegetation and animals, human vital energy and sometimes destiny. Zana e Madhe ("the Great Zana") is thought to have been an Illyrian goddess, equivalent of the Ancient Greek Artemis and Roman Diana.

claims.statement: Folk belief considers the zana extraordinarily courageous (hence the Albanian expression trim si zana), and they protect warriors like Pallas Athena of Ancient Greece.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat zana dianggap luar biasa berani (sehingga ada ungkapan Albania trim si zana) dan melindungi para pejuang seperti Pallas Athena dari Yunani Kuno.
claims.quote: The zana are considered in folk beliefs to be extraordinary courageous (thus the Albanian expression trim si zana) and they confer their protection on warriors similarly to Pallas Athena of Ancient Greece.

claims.statement: The Illyrian Thana (a nymph, fairy or deity named in Roman-era votive inscriptions) is traditionally considered the precursor of the Albanian Zana and a cognate of Latin Diāna.
claims.statement_id: Thana dari Iliria (nama nimfa, peri, atau dewa dalam prasasti nazar zaman Romawi) secara tradisional dianggap cikal bakal Zana Albania, dan dipandang seasal dengan Diāna dalam bahasa Latin.
claims.quote: the Illyrian Thana (the name of a nymph, fairy or deity, attested in votive inscriptions of the Roman era) is traditionally considered the precursor of the Albanian Zana. The theonym is also regarded as a cognate and equivalent of the Latin Diāna.

claims.statement: In Northern Albania and Kosovo every mountain is said to have its own zana, appearing as a fair maiden bathing in mountain streams; the original zana is escorted by three wild goats with golden horns.
claims.statement_id: Di Albania utara dan Kosovo setiap gunung dikatakan punya zana sendiri, yang tampak sebagai gadis cantik mandi di sungai gunung; zana asli dikawal tiga kambing liar bertanduk emas.
claims.quote: In Northern Albania and Kosovo every mountain is said to have its own zana, who appeared as a fair maiden found bathing naked in mountain streams.

claims.statement: The zana is believed to have the power to petrify humans with a glance.
claims.statement_id: Zana dipercaya memiliki kekuatan membuat manusia membatu dengan tatapannya.
claims.quote: The zana is believed to have the power to petrify humans with a glance

claims.statement: Similar Albanian nymph-like figures are Ora, Bardha, Shtojzovalle, Mira and Fatí.
claims.statement_id: Tokoh mitologi Albania serupa yang mirip nimfa adalah Ora, Bardha, Shtojzovalle, Mira, dan Fatí.
claims.quote: Similar Albanian mythological figures with nymph-like attributes are: Ora, Bardha, Shtojzovalle, Mira and Fatí.

claims.statement: In Albanian folklore the original Zana is escorted by three wild goats with golden horns.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat Albania, Zana asli dikawal tiga kambing liar bertanduk emas.
claims.quote: In Albanian folklore the original Zana is escorted by three wild goats with golden horns.

claims.statement: The zanas are thought to have watched the speeches at the League of Prizren in 1878.
claims.statement_id: Para zana dipercaya menyaksikan pidato-pidato di Liga Prizren tahun 1878.
claims.quote: Zanat mendohet se kanë vëzhguar fjalimet në Lidhjen e Prizrenit të vitit 1878.

claims.statement: According to Hieronim Malecki's catalogue (16th century, XVI), Autrimps is the Old Prussian god of seas and lakes, identified with the master of magic, the water god Patrimps-Andaj.
claims.statement_id: Menurut katalog Hieronim Malecki (abad ke-16, XVI), Autrimps adalah dewa laut dan danau Prusia Kuno, disamakan dengan penguasa sihir, dewa perairan Patrimps-Andaj.
claims.quote: według katalogu Hieronima Maleckiego (XVI w) staropruski bóg mórz i jezior; tożsamy z władcą magii, bogiem wód Patrimpsem-Andajem.

claims.statement: Autrimpas is the ancient Prussian sea god.
claims.statement_id: Autrimpas adalah dewa laut Prusia Kuno.
claims.quote: Autrimpas – senovės prūsų jūros dievas.

claims.statement: In 16th–17th-century (XVI, XVII) sources he is called Antrimpus or Natrimpe, described as god of the sea and wide waters, and compared with the Roman Neptune.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber abad ke-16 hingga ke-17 (XVI, XVII) ia disebut Antrimpus atau Natrimpe, digambarkan sebagai dewa laut dan perairan luas, dan dibandingkan dengan Neptunus (Neptune) Romawi.
claims.quote: XVI a. – XVII a. šaltiniuose jis vadinamas Antrimpu, Natrimpu, apibūdinamas kaip jūros ir plačių vandenų dievas. Lyginamas su romėnų Neptūnu.

claims.statement: Vladimir Toporov derives Autrimps and Patrimps from the fertility god Trimps.
claims.statement_id: Vladimir Toporov menurunkan Autrimps dan Patrimps dari dewa kesuburan Trimps.
claims.quote: Vladimiras Toporovas Autrimpą ir Patrimpą kildina iš vaisingumo dievo Trimpo.

claims.statement: According to the Lithuanian Mythology Encyclopedia, Autrimpas (also Autrimpum, Natrimpe, Aurimpus, Autrymius) is an ancient Prussian sea god.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Mitologijos enciklopedija Lituania, Autrimpas (juga Autrimpum, Natrimpe, Aurimpus, Autrymius) adalah dewa laut Prusia Kuno.
claims.quote: Autrimpas (Autrimpum, Natrimpe, Aurimpus, Autrymius), senovės prūsų jūrų dievas.

claims.statement: The name Natrimpe was first recorded in a report from the Bishop of Warmia to the pope in 1418.
claims.statement_id: Nama Natrimpe pertama kali tercatat dalam laporan uskup Warmia kepada paus pada 1418.
claims.quote: Natrimpe vardu pirmą kartą užfiksuotas 1418 Varmės vyskupo pranešime popiežiui.

claims.statement: In the 16th century he was identified with the Roman Neptune and mentioned alongside Patrimpas (god of flowing waters) and Bardaitis (god of seafaring).
claims.statement_id: Pada abad ke-16 ia disamakan dengan Neptunus Romawi dan disebut bersama Patrimpas (dewa air mengalir) dan Bardaitis (dewa pelayaran).
claims.quote: XVI a. tapatinamas su romėnų Neptūnu ir minimas greta Patrimpo (tekančių vandenų dievo), Bardaičio (jūreivystės dievo).

claims.statement: These gods may have been associated with one another because of their link with waters.
claims.statement_id: Dewa-dewa ini mungkin dikaitkan satu sama lain karena hubungan mereka dengan perairan.
claims.quote: Šie dievai galėjo būti siejami dėl jų ryšio su vandenimis.

claims.statement: According to the Lithuanian General Encyclopedia, 16th-17th-century sources call him Antrimpus or Natrimpus, describe him as god of the sea and wide waters, and compare him with the Roman Neptune.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Visuotinė lietuvių enciklopedija, dalam sumber abad ke-16 dan ke-17 ia disebut Antrimpus atau Natrimpus, digambarkan sebagai dewa laut dan perairan luas, dan dibandingkan dengan Neptunus Romawi.
claims.quote: senovės prūsų jūros dievas. 16–17 a. šaltiniuose vadinamas Antrimpu, Natrimpu, apibūdinamas kaip jūros ir plačių vandenų dievas; lyginamas su romėnų Neptūnu.

claims.statement: V. Toporov derives Autrimpas (and Patrimpas) from the fertility god Trimpas.
claims.statement_id: V. Toporov menurunkan Autrimpas (dan Patrimpas) dari dewa kesuburan Trimpas.
claims.quote: V. Toporovas kildina Autrimpą (ir Patrimpą) iš vaisingumo dievo Trimpo.

claims.statement: In Catalan mythology, Comte Estruch, also Arnald Estruc or Wilfred Estruch, was a 12th-century Catalan noble who became a vampire.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Katalan, Comte Estruch, juga disebut Arnald Estruc atau Wilfred Estruch, adalah bangsawan Katalan abad ke-12 yang menjadi vampir.
claims.quote: In Catalan mythology, Comte Estruch—also known as Arnald Estruc or Wilfred Estruch—was a 12th-century Catalan noble who became a vampire.

claims.statement: This legend is called the oldest vampire tale in European history and one of the few Iberian myths about vampirism.
claims.statement_id: Legenda ini disebut kisah vampir tertua dalam sejarah Eropa dan salah satu dari sedikit mitos Iberia tentang vampirisme.
claims.quote: This legend is the oldest vampire tale in European history and is one of the few Iberian myths associated with vampirism.

claims.statement: King Alfons II of Aragon sent the old noble Arnald Estruc to Llers Castle (Alt Empordà) to fight paganism and witchcraft, where he was killed in 1173; afterwards he sucked villagers' blood and impregnated young women, who after nine months bore monstrous newborns dead at birth.
claims.statement_id: Raja Alfons II dari Aragon mengirim bangsawan tua Arnald Estruc ke Kastel Llers (Alt Empordà) untuk memerangi paganisme dan sihir, dan ia terbunuh di sana pada 1173; setelah itu ia mengisap darah penduduk dan menghamili perempuan muda, yang setelah sembilan bulan melahirkan bayi mengerikan yang mati saat lahir.
claims.quote: King Alfons II of Aragon sent the old noble Count Arnald Estruc to fight paganism and witchcraft at Llers Castle (Alt Emporda) where the Count was killed in 1173. ... Count Estruch sucked blood from the villagers in the area and seduced and impregnated young women. After nine months, these women would give birth to monstrous newborns who were dead at birth.

claims.statement: In one version he was slain by an elderly nun; in others a Jewish hermit killed him with ancient Kabbalah rituals; the castle was destroyed in the Spanish Civil War.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu versi ia dibunuh seorang biarawati tua; dalam versi lain seorang pertapa Yahudi membunuhnya dengan ritual kuno Kabbalah; kastelnya hancur dalam Perang Saudara Spanyol.
claims.quote: In one version, he was slain by an elderly nun. In other versions, a Jewish hermit killed the count using ancient rituals from the Kabbalah. The castle was destroyed during the Spanish Civil War .

claims.statement: Comte Estruc is a literary character in Salvador Sáinz's novel Estruch (1991).
claims.statement_id: Comte Estruc adalah tokoh sastra dalam novel karya Salvador Sáinz, Estruch (1991).
claims.quote: El Comte Estruc és un personatge literari que apareix a la novel·la de l'escriptor Salvador Sáinz Estruch (1991).

claims.statement: Historians generally deny the truth of the supposed legend and hold that there is no historical trace of Estruch; the author never proved the 12th-century source he claimed.
claims.statement_id: Para sejarawan umumnya menolak kebenaran legenda yang diklaim itu dan berpendapat tidak ada jejak sejarah sosok Estruch; penulisnya tidak pernah membuktikan sumber abad ke-12 yang ia klaim.
claims.quote: Malgrat que l'autor afirma que la seva obra es basa en una llegenda que ell mateix recuperà d'una història del segle xii, mai no n'ha establert la fidelitat ni n'ha aportat cap prova. ... fa que, en general, els historiadors neguin la veracitat de la suposada llegenda i sostinguin que no hi ha rastres històrics de la figura d'Estruch.

claims.statement: The dakhanavar is a vampire of Armenian folklore who protected the valley from intruders, first reported by Baron August von Haxthausen in his mid-19th-century account of Armenia and Russian Transcaucasia.
claims.statement_id: Dakhanavar adalah vampir dalam cerita rakyat Armenia yang melindungi lembah dari penyusup, pertama dicatat Baron August von Haxthausen dalam kisahnya tentang Armenia dan Transkaukasia Rusia pada pertengahan abad ke-19.
claims.quote: is a vampire in Armenian folklore who protected the valley from intruders, first reported by Baron August von Haxthausen in his mid-19th century account of Armenia and Russian Transcaucasia

claims.statement: The dakhanavar follows travellers until they rest, then attacks them asleep, typically going for their feet.
claims.statement_id: Dakhanavar membuntuti pelancong sampai mereka beristirahat, lalu menyerang saat mereka tidur, biasanya menyasar kaki mereka.
claims.quote: The Dakhanavar follows travelers until they stop for a rest, stalking their every move.  When they finally stop, the vampire attacks them in their sleep, typically going for their feet.

claims.statement: Per Haxthausen, a vampire called Dakhanavar once lived in a cave there and could not bear anyone entering the mountains or counting the valleys; anyone who tried had his blood sucked from his soles at night until he died.
claims.statement_id: Menurut catatan Haxthausen, di negeri itu pernah tinggal di sebuah gua vampir bernama Dakhanavar yang tidak tahan bila ada yang masuk ke pegunungan atau menghitung lembahnya; siapa pun yang mencoba diisap darahnya dari telapak kaki pada malam hari sampai mati.
claims.quote: There once dwelt in a cavern in this country a vampire, called Dakhanavar, who could not endure anyone to penetrate into these mountains or count their valleys. Everyone who attempted this had in the night his blood sucked by the monster, from the soles of his feet, until he died.

claims.statement: In one legend two men outwitted him by sleeping with their feet under each other's heads; thinking them one two-headed, footless being, the vampire fled the valley and was never heard from again.
claims.statement_id: Dalam satu legenda ia diakali dua lelaki yang tidur dengan kaki di bawah kepala yang lain; vampir itu mengira mereka satu makhluk berkepala dua tanpa kaki, lalu lari dari lembah dan tak terdengar lagi.
claims.quote: In one legend, he was outsmarted by two men who had already heard of the vampire's habits and slept with their feet under the other's head.  The vampire, thinking that they were one being with two heads and no feet, ran from the valley and was never heard from again.

claims.statement: The dakhanavar, also Dashnavar, is a vampire of ancient Armenian mythology living in the Ultish Alto-tem mountains, famed for never killing the people who lived on his land.
claims.statement_id: Dakhanavar, juga Dashnavar (Դախանավար), dalam mitologi Armenia kuno adalah vampir yang tinggal di Pegunungan Ultish Alto-tem dan terkenal tidak pernah membunuh penduduk di tanahnya.
claims.quote: Даханавар, также Дашнавар (арм. Դախանավար) — в древнеармянской мифологии вампир, который проживает в горах Ултиш Альто-тэм. Он прославился тем, что никогда не убивал жителей, которые жили на его землях.

claims.statement: By legend the dakhanavar held 366 valleys and never let strangers in; with inhuman strength he protected the people for years, keeping enemies from passing the Ultish Alto-tem gorge to conquer Armenia.
claims.statement_id: Menurut legenda, Dakhanavar menguasai 366 lembah dan tidak pernah membiarkan orang asing masuk; dengan kekuatan luar biasa ia bertahun-tahun melindungi rakyat dengan mencegah musuh melewati ngarai Ultish Alto-tem dan menaklukkan Armenia.
claims.quote: Даханавар, по легенде, владел 366 долинами и никогда не пускал к себе чужаков. Обладая нечеловеческой мощью, он долгие годы защищал людей, не давая врагам пройти горное ущелье Ултиш Альто-тэм и захватить Армению

claims.statement: In Finnish mythology a haltija is the supernatural inhabitant of a place and protector of living beings, living invisibly but able to show itself to humans.
claims.statement_id: Dalam mitologi Finlandia, haltija adalah penghuni gaib suatu tempat dan pelindung makhluk hidup, hidup di lingkungan tak terlihat tetapi dapat menampakkan diri kepada manusia.
claims.quote: In Finnish mythology, a haltija is a supernatural inhabitant of a specific place and a protector of living beings, living in an invisible environment but able to show themselves to humans.

claims.statement: A haltija could be the supernatural original inhabitant and guardian of a place or the original mother of an animal species; a person buried at home could also become one.
claims.statement_id: Haltija bisa berupa penghuni asli dan penjaga gaib suatu tempat atau ibu asal suatu jenis hewan; orang yang meninggal dan dikuburkan di rumahnya juga bisa menjadi haltija.
claims.quote: A haltija could be the supernatural original inhabitant and guardian of a place or the original mother of an animal species. A person who died and was buried to their home could also become a haltija.

claims.statement: A local haltija is a solitary creature protecting its home, nature and peace; a haltija of an animal species keeps it alive by returning dead animals to the earth.
claims.statement_id: Haltija suatu tempat adalah makhluk penyendiri yang melindungi rumah, alam, dan ketenangannya; haltija suatu jenis hewan menjaga kelangsungan jenis itu dengan mengembalikan hewan mati ke bumi.
claims.quote: A haltija of a locality is a solitary creature who protects their home, its nature and peace. A haltija of an animal species protects their continued existence by returning dead animals back to earth.

claims.statement: Risto Pulkkinen described a jumala as ruling a wider concept such as water and a haltija as more local, ruling a specific body of water; he held that Finnish paganism had few jumala but a wide variety of haltija.
claims.statement_id: Risto Pulkkinen menggambarkan jumala sebagai penguasa konsep luas seperti air, sedangkan haltija lebih setempat, menguasai satu perairan; menurutnya hanya sedikit jumala dalam paganisme Finlandia tetapi ada banyak sekali jenis haltija.
claims.quote: Risto Pulkkinen ... described a jumala as a being who rules over a wider concept, such as water, while a haltija is more localized, ruling over a specific body of water. According to him, there is only a small number of beings in Finnish paganism which could be called jumala, but a wide variety of haltija beings.

claims.statement: The word may derive from Proto-Norse *halđiaz ("hold") or from the Finnish verb hallita, "to rule"; Lauri Harvilahti suggested a Baltic origin in žaltys, "grass snake", seen as a household spirit.
claims.statement_id: Kata ini mungkin berasal dari Proto-Nordik *halđiaz ("memegang"), atau dari kata kerja Finlandia hallita, "menguasai"; Lauri Harvilahti mengusulkan asal Baltik žaltys, "ular rumput", yang dianggap roh rumah.
claims.quote: The word is possibly derived from the Proto-Norse *halđiaz or *halđia- ... It can also be derived from the Finnish verb hallita, which means "to rule", "to command", "to master". ... Lauri Harvilahti suggested a Baltic origin: žaltys means a "grass snake", which was considered a household spirit.

claims.statement: Haltijat or haltiat are mythological beings believed to rule or protect a place or a being.
claims.statement_id: Haltija atau haltia adalah makhluk mitologis yang dipercaya menguasai atau melindungi suatu tempat atau makhluk.
claims.quote: Haltijat eli haltiat ovat mytologisia taruolentoja, joiden on uskottu hallitsevan tai suojelevan jotakin paikkaa tai olentoa.

claims.statement: Haltijat are thought usually to live unseen by humans, but sometimes they can show themselves.
claims.statement_id: Haltija dianggap biasanya hidup tak terlihat oleh manusia, tetapi kadang dapat menampakkan diri.
claims.quote: Haltijoiden katsotaan elävän yleensä ihmisille näkymättömissä, mutta toisinaan ne voivat näyttäytyä.

claims.statement: Kopala (კოპალა) is a traditional hero or demigod revered in the Pshavi highlands of Georgia.
claims.statement_id: K'op'ala (Kopala, კოპალა) adalah pahlawan tradisional atau setengah dewa yang dihormati di dataran tinggi Pshavi, Georgia.
claims.quote: (Georgian: კოპალა) is a traditional hero or demigod revered in the highlands of Pshavi in Georgia.

claims.statement: He once had a boulder-throwing contest with the devebi (ogres); the god Kviria whipped the stone so it landed on the fortress of Tsikhetgori.
claims.statement_id: Ia pernah beradu melempar batu besar melawan para devebi (raksasa); dewa Kviria memecut batunya sehingga mendarat di benteng Tsikhetgori.
claims.quote: he once was in a boulder-throwing contest against a number of devebi, or ogres, to see who could throw a boulder the furthest. ... the god "Kviria" struck the boulder with his whip, causing it to fly further than the ogre's boulder, and it landed on top of the ogres' fortress of Tsikhetgori.

claims.statement: After their defeat in the ensuing battle against Kopala and his companion Iakhsar, the surviving ogres retreated underground, letting people settle the area undisturbed.
claims.statement_id: Setelah kalah dalam pertempuran melawan K'op'ala dan rekannya Iakhsar, sisa raksasa mundur ke bawah tanah sehingga manusia dapat menetap di daerah itu tanpa gangguan.
claims.quote: As a result of their defeat in an ensuing battle that Kopala fought with his companion "Iakhsar", the surviving ogres retreated underground, allowing mankind to settle in the area undisturbed.

claims.statement: K'op'ala is a pre-Christian community deity of the eastern Georgian mountains; in Georgian mythology a local god of the Pshavs (Pkhovels) from the khvtisshvili (children of God).
claims.statement_id: K'op'ala adalah dewa komunitas pra-Kristen di pegunungan Georgia timur; dalam mitologi Georgia ia dewa setempat orang Pshav (Pkhovel) dari golongan khvtisshvili (anak-anak Tuhan).
claims.quote: კოპალა — წინაქრისტიანული სათემო ღვთაება აღმოსავლეთ საქართველოს მთაში. ქართულ მითოლოგიაში ფშაველთა (ფხოველთა) ლოკალური ღვთაება ხვთისშვილთა რიგიდან.

claims.statement: His main shrines were in Pshavi and Khevsureti; the sanctuary in the Likoki valley stands on Mount Karati; Khevsurs believed venerating the Karati cross protects from drowning and avalanches.
claims.statement_id: Tempat pemujaan utamanya di Pshavi dan Khevsureti; tempat suci di lembah Likoki berdiri di puncak Gunung Karati; menurut kepercayaan orang Khevsur, memuja salib Karati melindungi dari tenggelam dan tertimbun longsoran salju.
claims.quote: მისი ძირითადი სამლოცველო იყო ფშავსა (სოფ. უძილაურთა) და ხევსურეთში (ლიქოკის ხეობა, ჭალაისოფელი). სალოცავი ლიქოკის ხეობაში, კარატის მთის მწვერვალზე დგას. ხევსურთა რწმენით, კარატის ჯვრის თაყვანისცემა იცავს წყალში დახრჩობისგან და ზვავში მოყოლისგან

claims.statement: As a community deity, K'op'ala protected his followers in hardship, accompanied them on campaigns and helped them.
claims.statement_id: Sebagai dewa komunitas, K'op'ala melindungi para pengikutnya dalam kesulitan, menyertai mereka dalam peperangan, dan menolong mereka.
claims.quote: კოპალა, როგორც სათემო ღვთაება, თავის ყმებს მფარველობდა გასაჭირში, თან ახლდა ლაშქრობებში და ხელს უმართავდა.

claims.statement: The lamia is a giant evil dragon-like female being of Bulgarian myth, living at the bottom of lakes, rivers and seas, hoarding gems and gold in caves; Bulgarian heroes easily behead her, but if the head is put on a bull's horn, after forty days head and horn grow back into a serpent.
claims.statement_id: Lamia (Bulgaria: Ламя) adalah makhluk betina raksasa mirip naga yang jahat dalam mitos Bulgaria, tinggal di dasar danau, sungai, dan laut, menyimpan permata dan emas di gua; pahlawan Bulgaria mudah memenggalnya, tetapi bila kepalanya ditancapkan pada tanduk banteng, setelah empat puluh hari kepala dan tanduk menyatu menjadi ular lagi.
claims.quote: — гигантское злое драконообразное существо женского пола в мифах и легендах болгар. Ламии обитают на дне озёр, рек, морей. В своих пещерах часто хранят драгоценные камни и золотые клады. Несмотря на грозный вид Ламии, болгарские герои легко расправляются с ней, отрубив голову. Однако если отрезанную голову насадить на бычий рог, то через сорок дней голова и рог вновь срастаются в змею.

claims.statement: The lamia is a Slavic demon of Bulgarian mythology arising from a snake whose head was cut off and stuck on an ox horn; after 40 (forty) days head and horn grew together into a lamia.
claims.statement_id: Lamia (Lamja) adalah iblis Slavia dalam mitologi Bulgaria yang berasal dari ular yang kepalanya dipenggal dan ditancapkan pada tanduk lembu; setelah 40 hari (empat puluh) kepala dan tanduk menyatu menjadi lamia.
claims.quote: demon słowiański z mitologii bułgarskiej, pochodzący od węża, któremu odcięto głowę i zatknięto ją na róg wołu (po 40 dniach głowa i róg zrastały się i tak powstawała lamia).

claims.statement: The lamia is usually shown as a giant female serpent-like being with scaly wings, yellow scales, sharp claws and teeth, usually a dog's head on a snake's neck, sometimes three- or nine-headed.
claims.statement_id: Lamia biasanya digambarkan sebagai makhluk betina mirip ular berukuran raksasa, bersayap sisik, bersisik kuning, bercakar dan bergigi tajam, biasanya berkepala anjing di leher ular, kadang berkepala tiga atau sembilan.
claims.quote: Чаще всего Ламию изображают женственным змееподобным существом гигантских размеров, с чешуйчатыми крыльями, жёлтой чешуей, острыми когтями и зубами. Чаще всего имеет одну собачью голову на змеиной шее, но изредка её изображают трёхглавой или девятиглавой.

claims.statement: She is always hungry and thirsty for blood, sometimes damming rivers to cause drought and demanding human sacrifice to end it.
claims.statement_id: Ia selalu lapar dan haus darah, kadang membendung sungai sehingga terjadi kekeringan, dan menuntut korban manusia untuk mengakhirinya.
claims.quote: Она постоянно голодна и жаждет крови, иногда Ламия перекрывает русла рек, вызывая засухи, и требует людских жертвоприношений для их окончания.

claims.statement: In folk art the lamia was also shown as dark fog or a strong destructive wind; her mouth is so huge she can swallow a person alive.
claims.statement_id: Dalam seni rakyat lamia juga digambarkan sebagai kabut gelap atau angin kencang yang merusak; mulutnya sangat besar sehingga dapat menelan manusia hidup-hidup.
claims.quote: В народном творчестве Ламий изображали также в виде темного тумана или сильного, разрушительного ветра. Ламия имеет огромный рот, что позволяет ей проглотить человека живьём, когда она голодна.

claims.statement: The lamia was the zmey's antagonist; they were at constant war, the zmey defending the harvest and the lamia wishing to destroy it.
claims.statement_id: Lamia adalah lawan zmey; keduanya terus berperang, zmey membela panen dan lamia ingin menghancurkannya.
claims.quote: Lamia była antagonistką zmeja. Zmej i lamia byli w nieustającej wojnie – zmej bronił urodzaju, a lamia chciała go unicestwić.

claims.statement: The legend of Saint George (Georgi) killing the lamia was widespread; after he slew her with his spear she vanished and the saint came to be venerated; belief in the lamia faded early, as late 19th-century (XIX) records show.
claims.statement_id: Legenda tentang Santo Georgi yang membunuh lamia tersebar luas; setelah ia membunuhnya dengan tombak, lamia lenyap dan santo itu mulai dihormati; kepercayaan kepada lamia memudar cukup awal, seperti terlihat dari catatan akhir abad ke-19 (XIX).
claims.quote: Szeroko rozpowszechniona była także legenda o świętym Georgim, który zabija lamię (w polskiej wersji – święty Jerzy zabijający smoka). Po tym jak święty Georgi zabił ją swoją kopią, lamia przepadła i za to zaczęto czcić tego świętego. Wiara w lamię zanikła dość wcześnie, o czym świadczą przekazy z końca XIX wieku.

claims.statement: Maaemä (Finnish) or Maaema (Estonian) is a goddess or the earth itself in Finnish and Estonian mythologies; she is sometimes called Ukko's wife, but this is not certain.
claims.statement_id: Maaemä (Finlandia) atau Maaema (Estonia) adalah dewi atau bumi itu sendiri dalam mitologi Finlandia dan Estonia; ia kadang disebut istri Ukko, tetapi hal itu tidak pasti.
claims.quote: (Finnish) or Maaema (Estonian) is a goddess or earth itself in Finnish and Estonian mythologies. She is sometimes called the wife of Ukko but this is not certain.

claims.statement: In runic songs the earth itself is sometimes called maaemä, "earth mother", and set against a father in the sky, Ukko.
claims.statement_id: Dalam lagu rune, bumi sendiri kadang disebut maaemä, "ibu bumi", dan kadang dipertentangkan dengan bapa di langit atau Ukko.
claims.quote: In runic songs, the earth itself is sometimes called maaemä 'earth mother'. ... Maaemä is sometimes set as the opposite of a father in the sky or Ukko

claims.statement: A South Savo runic song invokes her as the one who raised snakes from the ground; a North Savo song tells how the Mistress of Earth brushed her hair and a snake formed from a bristle.
claims.statement_id: Lagu rune dari Savo Selatan memanggilnya sebagai dia yang membangkitkan ular dari tanah; lagu dari Savo Utara mengisahkan Nyonya Bumi menyisir rambut dan dari sehelai bulu sikat terbentuk ular.
claims.quote: A South Savo runic song invokes her, calling her the one who raised snakes from the ground. A North Savo runic song explains how the Mistress of Earth brushed her hair and from a bristle of the brush, a snake was formed.

claims.statement: A Kainuu runic song describes a stone as something that "tastes like the earth of Maatar" (Lady Earth).
claims.statement_id: Lagu rune dari Kainuu menggambarkan batu sebagai sesuatu yang "berasa seperti tanah Maatar" (Nyonya Bumi).
claims.quote: A Kainuu runic song describes a stone as something that "tastes like the earth of Maatar"

claims.statement: Maaema is the dearest and most honoured spirit of the land, also called the land's protector.
claims.statement_id: Maaema adalah roh bumi yang paling dikasihi dan dihormati, juga disebut pelindung tanah.
claims.quote: Maaema on kõige armsam ja austatud maa haldjas üldse. Teda kutsutakse ka maakaitsjaks.

claims.statement: Since the earth is the dearest mother who turns no one away, the homeless are her special wards.
claims.statement_id: Karena bumi adalah ibu terkasih yang tak mengusir siapa pun, para tunawisma menjadi asuhan khususnya.
claims.quote: Kuna maa on kõige armsam ema, kes ei aja kedagi enda juurest ära, siis kodutud on tema erilised hoolealused.

claims.statement: To protect maaema no one could poke the ground with a knife, which pierces her heart, and throwing hot water scalds her head; pulling grass was forbidden too, since it pulled her hair.
claims.statement_id: Untuk melindungi maaema, orang dilarang menusuk tanah dengan pisau karena itu melukai hatinya, dan menyiram air panas ke tanah membakar kepalanya; mencabut rumput juga dilarang karena sama dengan mencabut rambutnya.
claims.quote: Maaema kaitsmiseks ei tohtinud keegi noaga maas surkida, sest siis sorgitakse maaema südames ning tulist vett maha visates kõrvetatakse maaema pead. Ka rohukitkumine oli keelatud, sest siis kitkuti maaema juukseid.

claims.statement: A piru is a fiend or demon of Finnish mythology; the word comes from Proto-Finnic *piru, "devil, demon", with cognates in Karelian, Ingrian and Estonian; its ultimate origin is unknown.
claims.statement_id: Piru adalah iblis atau setan dalam mitologi Finlandia; katanya diwarisi dari Proto-Finnik *piru, "setan, iblis", berkerabat dengan bahasa Karelia, Ingria, dan Estonia; asal akhirnya tidak diketahui.
claims.quote: A piru is a fiend or demon in Finnish mythology. The word is inherited from Proto-Finnic *piru* ‘devil, demon’, with cognates in Karelian, Ingrian and Estonian; its ultimate origin is unknown.

claims.statement: In folklore a piru is often a nasty forest spirit with whom a smart aleck wins or loses a battle of wits, giving or receiving a forfeit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam cerita rakyat, piru sering tampil sebagai roh hutan jahat yang diajak beradu akal oleh orang cerdik, yang menang atau kalah dan memberi atau menerima taruhan.
claims.quote: In folklore, a piru is often featured as a nasty spirit of the forest with which a smart aleck either wins or loses a battle of wits, giving or receiving a forfeit in return.

claims.statement: Poltergeist and haunting phenomena are often called "pirus"; the Devil may be called Piru or Pääpiru, the main piru.
claims.statement_id: Gejala poltergeist dan rumah berhantu sering disebut "piru"; Iblis dapat disebut Piru atau Pääpiru, piru utama.
claims.quote: En molts casos, els poltergeist i fenòmens d'aparicions es descriuen com pirus. Sovint el Diable és anomenat també Piru o Pääpiru, el piru major.

claims.statement: In Finnish folk tradition a piru is either a servant of the Devil or another lesser evil being (a demon), or the Devil himself.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan rakyat Finlandia, piru adalah pelayan Iblis atau makhluk jahat yang lebih rendah (demon), atau Iblis itu sendiri.
claims.quote: Piru on suomalaisessa kansanperinteessä joko paholaista palveleva tai muutoin vähäisempi paha olento eli demoni, tai itse paholainen.

claims.statement: Pirus can strike suddenly and possess people; the possessed may act madly, fall ill or change personality entirely, and a skilled exorcist can remove the possession.
claims.statement_id: Piru dapat menyerang tiba-tiba dan merasuki manusia; orang yang dirasuki bisa berperilaku gila, jatuh sakit, atau berubah kepribadian, dan rasukan dapat diusir oleh pengusir setan yang ahli.
claims.quote: Ne voivat iskeä äkkiarvaamatta ja riivata ihmisiä eli asettua ihmiseen asumaan. Riivattu ihminen saattaa käyttäytyä hullusti tai sairastua, tai hänen persoonallisuutensa voi muuttua täysin. Riivauksen voi poistaa asiansa osaava manaaja.

claims.statement: "Piru" is also a mild swearword in Finnish.

claims.statement: Polkan or Palkan is a half-human, half-horse creature (half-dog in some variants) of Russian folktales, known for his immense power and speed.
claims.statement_id: Polkan (Полкан) atau Palkan adalah makhluk setengah manusia setengah kuda (dalam beberapa varian setengah anjing) dari dongeng Rusia, terkenal karena kekuatan dan kecepatannya.
claims.quote: is a half-human, half-horse creature (in some variants, half-dog) from Russian folktales, known for his immense power and speed.

claims.statement: In folk etymology his name is read as polukon, "half-horse".
claims.statement_id: Dalam etimologi rakyat namanya ditafsirkan sebagai polukon, "setengah kuda".
claims.quote: In folk etymology, his name is interpreted as polukon (Russian: полуконь), meaning 'half-horse'.

claims.statement: He first appears as the enemy of the hero Bova Korolevich but after a battle becomes Bova's loyal friend and ally, eventually dying fighting lions to protect Bova's wife and children.
claims.statement_id: Ia mula-mula musuh pahlawan Bova Korolevich, tetapi setelah bertarung menjadi sahabat dan sekutu setia Bova, lalu gugur melawan singa saat melindungi istri dan anak-anak Bova.
claims.quote: He initially appears as the enemy of the hero Bova Korolevich, but after a battle, he becomes Bova's loyal friend and ally. He eventually dies fighting lions while protecting Bova's wife and children.

claims.statement: The tale was extremely popular in Russia and entered folklore, appearing in many lubok prints and woodcuts; Alexander Pushkin used some of its elements in his fairy tales.
claims.statement_id: Kisah ini sangat populer di Rusia, menjadi bagian cerita rakyat, dan muncul dalam banyak lubok serta ilustrasi cukil kayu; Alexander Pushkin memakai beberapa unsurnya untuk dongengnya.
claims.quote: This tale was extremely popular in Russia and became part of Russian folklore, leading to numerous lubok prints containing the tale as well as woodcut illustrations. Alexander Pushkin in particular used some elements from the story for his own fairy tales.

claims.statement: Polkan has immense strength and speed and can bound great distances, "seven versts in one leap".
claims.statement_id: Polkan memiliki kekuatan dan kecepatan luar biasa dan dapat melompat sangat jauh, "tujuh versta dalam satu lompatan".
claims.quote: обладающий огромной силой и скоростью (может скачками перемещаться на большие расстояния — «семь вёрст за один скок»).

claims.statement: Polkan is based on Pulicane, a half-dog character in Andrea da Barberino's poem I Reali di Francia, once popular in the Slavonic world through prose translations; in modern Russia Polkan is a popular name for large dogs.
claims.statement_id: Polkan berasal dari Pulicane, tokoh setengah anjing dalam puisi Andrea da Barberino, I Reali di Francia, yang dulu populer di dunia Slavia lewat terjemahan prosa; di Rusia modern Polkan menjadi nama populer untuk anjing besar.
claims.quote: Polkan is originally based on Pulicane, a half-dog character from Andrea da Barberino's poem I Reali di Francia, which was once popular in the Slavonic world through prosaic translations.

claims.statement: The poroniec (plural porońce) is a hostile demon of Slavic mythology believed to arise from stillborn fetuses and improperly buried infants.
claims.statement_id: Poroniec (jamak porońce) adalah iblis jahat dari mitologi Slavia yang dipercaya berasal dari janin yang lahir mati dan dari jasad bayi yang tidak dikuburkan dengan benar.
claims.quote: is a hostile and malicious demon from Slavic mythology. They were believed to come into existence from stillborn fetuses, but also from improperly buried remains of children who had died during infancy.

claims.statement: Porońce were thought extremely powerful demons because of their unrealised potential of life.
claims.statement_id: Porońce dianggap iblis yang sangat kuat karena potensi kehidupan yang tak terwujud.
claims.quote: Porońce were considered to be extremely powerful demons, due to their potential of unrealized life.

claims.statement: Porońce were tied to many taboos for pregnant women, such as drawing water from a well, leaving home with an infant or having sex.
claims.statement_id: Porońce terkait banyak pantangan bagi perempuan hamil, seperti menimba air dari sumur, keluar rumah membawa bayi, atau berhubungan badan.
claims.quote: Porońce were associated with many taboos regarding pregnant women, such as drawing water from a well, leaving home with an infant, or engaging in sexual intercourse.

claims.statement: A stillborn fetus buried under the house threshold did not become a poroniec but a kłobuk, a protective house spirit.
claims.statement_id: Janin yang lahir mati tidak menjadi poroniec bila dikuburkan di bawah ambang pintu rumah, melainkan menjadi kłobuk, roh pelindung rumah.
claims.quote: A stillborn fetus did not turn into a poroniec if it was buried under the threshold of the house. Instead, it turned into a kłobuk ... – a protective house spirit.

claims.statement: In Slavic belief the poroniec is a malicious demon hostile to people, arising from the soul of a miscarried child or aborted fetus.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan Slavia, poroniec adalah iblis jahat yang memusuhi manusia, berasal dari jiwa bayi yang keguguran atau janin yang digugurkan.
claims.quote: w wierzeniach słowiańskich złośliwy i wrogi ludziom demon wywodzący się z duszy poronionego dziecka lub spędzonego płodu.

claims.statement: A poroniec is somewhat similar to the myling of Scandinavian folklore.
claims.statement_id: Poroniec agak mirip myling, makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Skandinavia.
claims.quote: A poroniec is somewhat similar to a being from Scandinavian folklore, the myling.

claims.statement: In the 2015 video game The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, one main quest revolves around the search for a botchling (poroniec in the original).
claims.statement_id: Dalam gim The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt tahun 2015, salah satu misi utama berkisar tentang pencarian botchling (poroniec dalam versi asli).
claims.quote: In the 2015 video game The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt, one of the main quests revolves around the search for a botchling (poroniec in the original version)

claims.statement: The sárkány ("dragon") is a legendary monster of Hungarian mythology, usually a scaly, winged, reptilian beast, sometimes a mixture of other beings.
claims.statement_id: Sárkány ("naga") adalah monster legendaris dalam mitologi Hungaria, biasanya berupa binatang reptil bersisik dan bersayap, kadang campuran makhluk lain.
claims.quote: ('dragon') is a legendary monster found in Hungarian mythology. It usually appears as a scaly, winged, reptilian beast, but in some cases it could be a mixture of other beings.

claims.statement: Hungarian sárkány is regarded as a loanword from Oghuric Turkic šaragan, "dragon", and may share a root with Hungarian sárga, "yellow".
claims.statement_id: Kata sárkány dianggap serapan dari bahasa Turkik Oghur šaragan, "naga", dan mungkin berakar sama dengan kata Hungaria sárga, "kuning".
claims.quote: Hungarian sárkány is regarded as a loanword from Oghuric Turkic (or "West Old Turkic") šaragan 'dragon' ... The word may be connected to the same root as occurs in Hungarian sárga ('yellow')

claims.statement: In Hungarian culture the sárkány is the ancient dragon of myth and legend, a divine monster and treasure guardian, usually a winged, scaly reptile.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kebudayaan Hungaria, sárkány adalah naga purba mitos dan legenda, monster ilahi dan penjaga harta, biasanya berwujud reptil bersayap dan bersisik.
claims.quote: A magyar kultúrkörben a sárkány mítoszok és legendák ősi sárkánya, isteni szörnyetege és a kincseket őrző lény, legtöbbször szárnyas, pikkelyes hüllő alakjában

claims.statement: Per the Hungarian ethnographic lexicon, the tarajos kígyó ("crested serpent") is a dreadful, supernaturally strong winged snake, horse-like in front and snake-like behind, hard-scaled, long-clawed and long-toothed, with a flaming crest, blowing sparks and spewing flame.
claims.statement_id: Menurut Magyar néprajzi lexikon, tarajos kígyó ("ular berjengger") adalah ular menakutkan berkekuatan gaib, bersayap, depannya mirip kuda dan belakangnya mirip ular, bersisik keras, berkuku dan bergigi panjang, berjengger menyala, meniup percikan dan memuntahkan api.
claims.quote: „A tarajos csúszó, tarajos kígyó félelmetes, természetfeletti erejű kígyó. Szárnyas alakú, elöl lóhoz, hátul kígyóhoz hasonlít, pikkelyes kemény bőrű, hosszú körmű, hosszú fogú, lángoló tarajú; szikrát fúj, lángot hány.

claims.statement: The sárkány, as the garabonciás's steed, is linked with storms, hail and treasure; it comes from a fish or snake hidden in a marsh or rock cleft and unseen by human eyes for seven years.
claims.statement_id: Sárkány, sebagai kuda tunggangan garabonciás, berhubungan dengan badai, hujan es, dan harta; ia lahir dari ikan atau ular yang tersembunyi di rawa atau tebing batu dan tujuh tahun tidak terlihat mata manusia.
claims.quote: „Sárkány, mint a garabonciás lova, kapcsolatban áll a viharral, jégesővel és a kincsekkel. Olyan halból vagy kígyóból lesz, amelyet mocsárban, kőszirtben elbújva hét évig emberi szem nem látott.”

claims.statement: The appearance of dragons was most often linked with destructive lightning storms, the thunder being the dragons raging in the sky.
claims.statement_id: Kemunculan naga paling sering dikaitkan dengan badai petir yang merusak, dan gemuruh guntur dianggap amukan naga di langit.
claims.quote: Általánosságban kijelenthető, hogy legtöbbször a pusztító, villámló viharokkal hozták összefüggésbe a sárkányok megjelenését, ahol a vihar mennydörgése tulajdonképpen a sárkányok tombolása volt az égben

claims.statement: Shubin is the mythological mining spirit; his legend spreads mainly in the mining towns of the Donbas on the Russia–Ukraine border; the spirit is usually good but can be wicked.
claims.statement_id: Shubin (Шубін) adalah roh tambang mitologis; legendanya terutama tersebar di kota-kota tambang Donbas di perbatasan Rusia dan Ukraina (Russia, Ukraine); roh ini biasanya baik tetapi bisa jahat.
claims.quote: is the mythological mining spirit. The legend of Shubin is distributed mainly in the mining towns of the Donbas region on the Russia–Ukraine border. In the north one can hear several legends about the spirit of the mines. The spirit is usually good, but can be wicked.

claims.statement: Explanations of the name: (1) the nickname of a miner whose soul walks the mine bottom in a fur coat with a torch, burning firedamp; (2) the cruel mine boss Shubin who killed workers underground; (3) the "shu-shu" sound of methane.
claims.statement_id: Penjelasan nama: (1) julukan penambang yang arwahnya berjalan di dasar tambang bermantel bulu membawa obor dan membakar gas tambang; (2) nama mandor kejam Shubin yang membunuh pekerja di bawah tanah; (3) bunyi metana "shu-shu".
claims.quote: (1) the nickname of a miner, whose soul, according to legend, walks in a fur coat at the bottom of the mine with a torch in his hand and burns the gas (firedamp); (2) the name of the cruel mining master Shubin, who slew workers underground; (3) the sound from methane (Shu-Shu), which often accumulates in the mines.

claims.statement: In September 2026, miners' tales about the guardian spirit Shubin were inscribed on the National Register of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Ukraine.
claims.statement_id: Pada September 2026, kisah penambang tentang roh pelindung Shubin dimasukkan ke Daftar Nasional Warisan Budaya Takbenda Ukraina.
claims.quote: In September 2026, miners' tales about the guardian spirit Shubin were inscribed on the National Register of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Ukraine.

claims.statement: Good Shubin, or just Shubin, is a figure of Donbas miners' folklore, a gnome-like mining spirit, "master of the mine" and patron of miners.
claims.statement_id: Shubin yang Baik, atau Shubin saja, adalah tokoh cerita rakyat penambang Donbas, roh tambang mirip gnome, "tuan tambang" dan pelindung para penambang.
claims.quote: Добрый Шу́бин, или просто Шубин — персонаж шахтёрского фольклора Донбасса, горняцкий дух, похожий на гнома, «хозяин шахты» и покровитель шахтёров.

claims.statement: Oral lore tells of good Shubin warning miners of coming disasters; he is imagined as a middle-aged man with a smoker's cough: "Hear the cough, run!"
claims.statement_id: Tuturan lisan menyebut Shubin yang baik memperingatkan penambang akan bencana; ia dibayangkan sebagai lelaki paruh baya dengan batuk perokok: "Dengar batuk, segera lari!"
claims.quote: Изустное предание гласит о добром Шубине, предупреждающим шахтёров о грядущих бедах. Образ Шубина представляется мужчиной средних лет с кашлем курильщика."Слышишь кашель-делай ноги!".

claims.statement: Beliefs about Shubin were recorded by folklore collectors, the writers Boris Gorbatov and Leonid Zharikov.
claims.statement_id: Kepercayaan tentang Shubin dicatat oleh pengumpul cerita rakyat, penulis Boris Gorbatov dan Leonid Zharikov.
claims.quote: Поверья о Шубине записали собиратели фольклора писатели Борис Горбатов и Леонид Жариков.

claims.statement: Besides the many Slavic gods and goddesses, the ancient Slavs believed in and revered many supernatural beings of nature, in various forms, whose names can be spelled differently by language and transliteration.
claims.statement_id: Selain banyak dewa dan dewi, bangsa Slavia kuno percaya dan menghormati banyak makhluk gaib di alam, yang beragam wujudnya, dan nama satu makhluk dapat dieja berbeda menurut bahasa dan sistem transliterasi.
claims.quote: Other than the many gods and goddesses of the Slavs, the ancient Slavs believed in and revered many supernatural beings that existed in nature. These supernatural beings in Slavic religion come in various forms, and the same name of any single being can be spelled or transliterated differently according to language and transliteration system.

claims.statement: The vila is a nymph-like fairy, identified as a nymph by the Greek historian Procopius; the name shares its root with Veles.
claims.statement_id: Vila adalah peri mirip nimfa yang oleh sejarawan Yunani Procopius disebut nimfa; namanya berakar sama dengan nama Veles.
claims.quote: is a fairy that is similar to a nymph, identified as a nymph by the Greek historian Procopius; their name comes from the same root as the name of Veles.

claims.statement: Vile are described as beautiful, eternally young, dressed in white, with thunder-flashing eyes, wings and blonde hair.
claims.statement_id: Vila digambarkan cantik, muda selamanya, berbaju putih, bermata berkilat seperti guntur, bersayap, dan berambut pirang. Bagi Slavia Selatan dan sebagian Slovakia, vila adalah makhluk perempuan yang umumnya bersifat baik.
claims.quote: They are described as beautiful, eternally young, dressed in white, with eyes flashing like thunder, and provided with wings, and blonde hair.

claims.statement: In the beliefs and folklore of the South Slavs and partly the Slovaks, the vila is a female mythological being with mainly positive qualities.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kepercayaan dan cerita rakyat Slavia Selatan dan sebagian Slovakia, vila adalah makhluk mitologis perempuan yang umumnya bersifat baik.
claims.quote: в верованиях и фольклоре южных славян и отчасти словаков женское мифологическое существо, наделяемое преимущественно положительными свойствами.

claims.statement: The vântoase are creatures of Romanian folklore, a sort of female spirit (iele), believed able to cause dust storms and powerful winds, like harpies.
claims.statement_id: Vântoase adalah makhluk dalam cerita rakyat Rumania, sejenis roh perempuan (iele), yang menurut kepercayaan dapat menimbulkan badai debu dan angin kencang, mirip harpy.
claims.quote: are creatures present in Romanian folklore, as a sort of female spirits (iele). Popular beliefs describe them as capable of causing dust storms and powerful winds, similar to harpies.

claims.statement: They live in forests, in the air and in deep lakes, travel in a special wagon, are believed able to attack children, and the only protection is the mysterious "grass of the winds".
claims.statement_id: Mereka tinggal di hutan, di udara, dan di danau dalam, bepergian dengan kereta khusus, dipercaya dapat menyerang anak-anak, dan satu-satunya perlindungan adalah "rumput angin" yang misterius.
claims.quote: They live in forests, in the air, in deep lakes, and use a special wagon for traveling. The Vântoase are also believed to be capable of attacking children, and the only protection against them is the mysterious "grass of the winds".

claims.statement: They are sometimes said to raise winds when they dance the hora.
claims.statement_id: Kadang dikatakan mereka menimbulkan angin saat menari hora.
claims.quote: Иногда говорят, что они вызывают ветры, когда танцуют хору.

claims.statement: The name vântoase (singular vântoasa) comes from the Romanian word vânt, "wind".
claims.statement_id: Nama vântoase (tunggal vântoasa) berasal dari kata Rumania vânt, "angin".
claims.quote: Имя вынтоасе (ед. ч. вынтоаса) происходит от румынского слова ветер (vânt).

claims.statement: They live in forests, in the air and in lakes and use winds to travel; in some legends they are servants of God.
claims.statement_id: Mereka tinggal di hutan, di udara, dan di danau, dan memakai angin untuk bepergian; dalam beberapa legenda mereka digambarkan sebagai pelayan Tuhan.
claims.quote: Они живут в лесах, в воздухе, в озёрах и используют ветры для путешествий. ... В некоторых легендах они представлены как слуги Господа.

claims.statement: They are believed able to attack children, and the only protection then is the mysterious grass of the winds.
claims.statement_id: Dipercaya mereka dapat menyerang anak-anak, dan satu-satunya perlindungan adalah rumput angin yang misterius.
claims.quote: Считается, что они могут нападать на детей. Единственным средством защиты от них в таком случае является загадочная трава ветров.
